questions.q: What happens during the prefill phase of LLM inference?
options: Output tokens are generated one at a time
The entire input prompt is processed in a single parallel forward pass, building the key/value tensors for attention
The model's weights are loaded from disk into GPU memory
The KV cache is deleted to free memory
questions.explain: Prefill processes every prompt token through every layer in parallel, building the key and value tensors (the KV cache) needed before generation can begin.

options: Because it never uses the GPU's matrix-multiplication units
Because all prompt tokens are processed together, keeping the GPU's math units busy and well-utilized
Because it only runs on CPU
Because it requires no memory access at all
questions.explain: Processing the whole prompt in parallel keeps the GPU's compute units continuously busy, which is the definition of compute-bound.

questions.q: Why is decode described as "memory-bound" rather than compute-bound?
options: Each decode step does a small amount of compute for one token, but spends significant time reading the growing KV cache from GPU memory
Decode uses no GPU memory at all
Decode processes the entire prompt again at every step
Decode is always faster than prefill for every request
questions.explain: Decode generates one token per step with little compute, but must repeatedly read the key/value tensors for all prior tokens out of memory, which under-utilizes the GPU's compute units.

questions.q: What is the KV cache's role in connecting prefill and decode?
options: It stores the raw text of the prompt for logging purposes
It stores the key/value tensors built during prefill, which decode reads and extends by one entry at every new token
It is only used during prefill and discarded before decode begins
It replaces the need for a tokenizer
questions.explain: Prefill builds the KV cache; decode reads the entire cache so far at each step and adds one new entry per generated token, growing the cache over the course of generation.

questions.q: Why do many LLM APIs price input (prompt) tokens differently from output (generated) tokens?
options: Input tokens are always free
Pricing is arbitrary and has no technical basis
Prefill (input tokens) and decode (output tokens) have different cost profiles, since one is compute-bound and the other memory-bound
Output tokens require no GPU at all
questions.explain: Because prefill and decode are bound by different resources and scale differently with load, their per-token cost to serve differs, which is reflected in differentiated pricing.
